senses.definition: A large area within a country that has a name and its own local government in many places.
senses.example: Ontario is a province in Canada.

senses.definition: Surrounded by land with no coast on the open ocean.
senses.example: Switzerland is landlocked, so a ship from the ocean has to use a river to reach it.

senses.definition: An area of deep enough water where boats can stay with some shelter from wind and waves.
senses.example: The ferry waited in the harbor while the weather improved.

senses.definition: To give someone or something a place to stay or hide.
senses.example: The old barn harbored several owls.

senses.definition: A long, narrow arm of the sea between steep slopes, formed when seawater filled a valley carved by ice.
senses.example: A boat sailed up a fjord between the steep mountains.

senses.definition: A broad low area or the whole area where water drains toward the same place.
senses.example: Rain in the river basin eventually reaches the same river.

senses.definition: A wide bowl or a sink that can hold water.
senses.example: We filled the basin with warm water to wash the mud from our hands.

senses.definition: A kind of rock made mostly of calcium carbonate, the material in many shells and corals.
senses.example: Water slowly made a cave in the limestone.

senses.definition: An area of land that stays very wet, where partly decayed plants build up in the ground.
senses.example: Some kinds of moss can grow in a bog.

senses.definition: A shallow body of water separated from a larger body of water by a strip of land or a reef.
senses.example: The narrow sandbar protected the lagoon from the ocean waves.

senses.definition: A hill or ridge of sand pushed together by wind or water.
senses.example: Beach grass helped keep sand from blowing away from the dune.

senses.definition: A narrow stretch of water that connects two larger bodies of water.
senses.example: The ship crossed the strait between the two islands.

senses.definition: A wide area of fairly flat land that stands higher than much of the land around it.
senses.example: From the edge of the plateau we looked down into the valley.

senses.definition: A narrow strip of land that joins two larger areas of land, with water on both sides.
senses.example: The Isthmus of Panama connects the land of Central and South America.

senses.definition: A wind pattern that changes direction with the seasons and often brings a rainy season.
senses.example: The summer monsoon brought heavy rain to the fields.

senses.definition: A place in a desert where water can reach the surface and plants can grow.
senses.example: Palm trees grew beside the water at the oasis.

senses.definition: A stream or river that flows into another stream or river.
senses.example: The creek is a tributary of the larger river downstream.

senses.definition: An area of land that stands high above the country around it.
senses.example: The days in the highlands were cooler than at the coast.

senses.definition: The height of a place or object compared with sea level or another starting level.
senses.example: The airplane reached a higher altitude as it climbed above the clouds.
